prompt_text: What is the best Airbnb or short term rental to book in Nashville for a family of four?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — but to give the single “best” option I’ll need a couple details. Before that, here’s quick guidance so you can find the ideal short‑term rental for a family of four.

Questions
- What are your exact travel dates (or season)?
- What’s your budget per night or total?
- Ages of the children?
- Will you have a car / need parking?
- Do you want to be walkable to restaurants/attractions, or prefer a quieter neighborhood and drive?

Neighborhoods that work best for families (pros/cons)
- 12 South — Charming bungalows, walkable to coffee/parks/shops, great for families. Generally quiet and safe.
- Germantown — Upscale, family‑friendly, close to downtown but calmer than Broadway.
- East Nashville — Trendy, more local vibe, parks and kid‑friendly restaurants; houses with yards common.
- Green Hills / Belle Meade — More residential, quieter, closer to shopping; good if you want space and parking.
- The Gulch — Walkable and stylish, but more condo/urban; good if you want to be close to dining and short drives to attractions.
- Avoid staying right on Broadway if you want quiet nights — it’s noisy until late.

What to filter/search for
- Entire home/apt (no shared spaces) with 2+ bedrooms (or 3 bedrooms if you want extra space).
- Washer/dryer, full kitchen, and free parking (or guaranteed parking spot).
- Family/kid friendly, crib/high chair available (if needed), fenced yard if small kids.
- Soundproofing or “quiet at night” mentioned in reviews.
- Superhost and overall review score 4.8+ for reliability.
- Clear cancellation policy and details about cleaning fees/extra guest fees.

Essential amenities & safety
- Air conditioning (Nashville summers are hot), heating (winter), reliable Wi‑Fi.
- Smoke & CO detectors, first aid kit, stair gates if needed.
- Pack-and-play/crib and high chair on request.
- Self check‑in (keypad) can be easier with kids.

Booking tips
- Read recent reviews (last 6–12 months) for noise, cleanliness, and responsiveness.
- Check bed layout/photos: where will the kids sleep? Sofabeds aren’t always comfortable.
- Message the host before booking to confirm parking, baby gear, and any neighborhood quirks.
- Compare total price (nightly + cleaning + service + taxes) not just nightly rate.
- Book early for peak times (Music City events, CMA Fest, etc.) — prices rise and availability drops.

If you want, I can:
- Search current Airbnb/short-term options and send top 3 picks for your dates and budget, or
- Recommend specific property examples in one of the neighborhoods above.

Tell me your dates, budget, and any must‑have amenities and I’ll find the best options.
